script: Gas Thief Revenge. I had a neighbor that would walk into my backyard, snatch my 5‑gal gas can for his mower, slide it into his car, and then drop it back when he was done. The can was always half‑empty every time I mowed; my mower only had a quart. I set up a laptop webcam with motion detection—no fancy security cams back then, so I was the DIY detective. I caught him five minutes after I'd left. But here's the thing, I was already thinking about how to make him pay. I started filling the can with pee every time I took a break, keeping the gas smell strong enough to fool a fool. I left it on the patio, made a big show of checking my car's fluid, packed a few bags, and told the neighbor I was heading out for a trip. I was hoping he'd take the bait and think he'd get a free gas run. I came back after an hour, and the thief was in his front yard, pulling on his mower's rope like a man about to have a stroke. His engine was red, cursing, and he drove a couple of blocks up the road—then the car just stalled. I checked the can on my patio, and it was empty again. Then it hit me—this was more than a gas thief; he had arrest warrants hanging over him. I applied for a sheriff's ride‑along program in his name, basically turning him into the very thing he'd been stealing from me. I was about to call the sheriff when…
